blocks.en: Proposition U.1 routes the amplification through the decision: a prediction survives quantization while the propagated perturbation stays inside the unquantized logit margin, the shift shrinks that margin while the activation quantization error does not, and the error itself is set by the step. We measure those quantities directly. The full-precision and the quantized network are run over the same inputs on the 5000 5000 -image subset, clean and all 15 15 corruptions at severity 5, with ‖ e ℓ ‖ \|e_{\ell}\| and the clipped fraction read at the sixteen recalibration interfaces using the deployed quantizer’s own step and clip range. Nothing adapts in this measurement, so every quantity is a per-image or per-element aggregate and does not depend on the stream order. The margin collapses under shift, from 3.78 3.78 to 2.05 2.05 , a drop of 46 % 46\% ; it is a property of the unquantized network, so it is one number for all four precisions. The activation quantization error does not follow it: ‖ e ℓ ‖ \|e_{\ell}\| moves by between − 3.2 % -3.2\% and + 2.2 % +2.2\% , and the clipped fraction falls at every bit-width, so the invariance is the granular term dominating, which is how Proposition U.1 splits 𝔼 ​ e ℓ , c 2 \mathbb{E}\,e_{\ell,c}^{2} and is consistent with the under-filling reported above. Across precisions ‖ e ℓ ‖ \|e_{\ell}\| instead tracks the step, rising monotonically from 2404 2404 at W8A8 to 17436 17436 at W3A3. The consequence is the predicted one: the fraction of predictions that are correct in full precision and wrong once quantized grows under shift at every precision, and it grows more the coarser the step, by 2.7 2.7 points at W8A8 against 19.5 19.5 at W3A3 (Table 30 ).

blocks.en: Table 32 isolates where the same correction is applied, with every variant at the deployed local configuration so that only the site differs. Before the quantizer, on the tensor it is about to round, is best at every bit-width. After the quantizer, on the dequantized tensor of the same interface, the codes the quantizer selects are those of the uncorrected activation: accuracy falls below No Adapt at W3A3 and W4A4 ( 27.98 27.98 and 47.01 47.01 against 28.35 28.35 and 47.30 47.30 ), because the drifted activation is clipped and coarsely rounded before any correction and the affine then rescales an already truncated signal, and it recovers 4.2 4.2 and 3.6 3.6 points at W6A6 and W8A8 ( 51.90 51.90 and 57.96 57.96 ), close to the Global-only branch. What the correction must change is which codes are used, not the values downstream of them. At the block output, the residual stream that no quantizer reads and the site at which normalization-statistics adaptation ( Schneider et al., 2020 ; Mirza et al., 2023 ) acts, the same affine reaches 32.18 32.18 , 50.32 50.32 , 51.14 51.14 and 57.29 57.29 : about half the gain of the quantizer-input placement ( 2.9 2.9 to 3.8 3.8 points over No Adapt against 4.8 4.8 to 7.0 7.0 ), within a point of our Global-only branch, which recalibrates only the head input, and 1.8 1.8 to 3.1 3.1 points below the quantizer inputs, a gap that widens as precision falls. Both placements away from the quantizer input therefore stop at the gain of aligning feature statistics, and the further 1.8 1.8 to 3.1 3.1 points appear only when the correction sits at the quantizer input. That is the site the code-distribution diagnostic (Figure 1 b) and Proposition 1 single out, and it is what separates QuAR from normalization-statistics adaptation applied to a quantized network. The block-output source moments are collected on the same calibration batches as the quantizer-input moments.

blocks.en: Appendix Q Measured test-time cost
blocks.zh: 附录Q 测量测试时间成本

blocks.en: All quantized models in this paper run in the PTQ4ViT and AdaLog PyTorch harness, which quantizes and dequantizes weights and activations in floating point, and every cost below is measured in that harness. What transfers to a deployment is therefore the ratio between methods rather than the absolute time, which Appendix R reproduces on a Jetson Orin Nano; the scope of an integer-only deployment is set out in Appendix T . Table 33 reports the measured per-method test-time cost at W6A6: forward-pass compute ( torch.profiler GFLOPs over the entire per-batch adaptation), peak GPU memory ( max_memory_allocated , per-process and hence independent of other GPU tenants), and wall-clock latency (per-image forward, timed on an idle NVIDIA TITAN RTX with one measurement at a time, as the median over 5 repetitions of the per-batch forward median across ∼ 50 {\sim}50 batches). QuAR stays in the single-forward tier on all three axes: it runs at 1.10 × 1.10\times the No Adapt latency, versus ∼ 2 × {\sim}2\times for the two-forward FOA/FOZO/ZOA, while peak memory is dominated by the frozen quantized backbone and batch activations, which QuAR does not add to. Applying the recalibration as a fresh tensor would: the blend needs the input and the corrected copy live at once, and at the mlp.fc2 interface that temporary is the 3072 3072 -wide MLP hidden state, four times the width of the other fifteen, which alone costs 148 148 MB at batch 64 64 . The deployed configuration instead applies the affine in place over batch slices ( --quar_local_chunk 2 ), which leaves 1601.08 1601.08 MB against No Adapt’s 1600.91 1600.91 MB, a 0.17 0.17 MB residual on top of the ∼ 170 {\sim}170 KB of stored statistics. This is bit-identical rather than an approximation, so no accuracy number depends on it: every operation is elementwise or a per-channel broadcast and the two reductions that span the tensor are taken before any slice is touched, and we confirmed it end to end, with top-1 and top-5 equal to the buffered path at batch 64 64 and batch 16 16 ( 46.80 / 69.50 46.80/69.50 and 46.54 / 69.30 46.54/69.30 on gaussian_noise ). T3A’s per-sample nearest-neighbour search adds latency not visible in matmul GFLOPs and grows with its support set, so its reported value is early-stream.

blocks.zh: 附录R Jetson Orin Nano的机床测量

blocks.en: The cost argument is about edge hardware, so we also ran it there: a Jetson Orin Nano Super devkit, Orin sm_87 , with the GPU sharing 7.31 7.31 GiB with the CPU. What transfers across a change of device is the ratio between methods rather than the absolute time, so Table 34 reports every side by ratio. The ordering is reproduced and the two-forward group again lands at ≈ 2 × {\approx}2\times . QuAR is cheaper in relative terms on the device than on the server, 1.071 × 1.071\times against 1.10 × 1.10\times . T3A moves the other way, 1.144 × 1.144\times against 1.36 × 1.36\times , because its per-sample nearest-neighbour search is bound by dispatch rather than arithmetic and the forward it is measured against is 8.6 × 8.6\times slower here.

blocks.en: Batch 16 16 is the informative column: it is the largest batch at which the backprop-based methods fit this board, so it is the only one where all four families sit on a single axis, and per-image latency there is within 3.9 % 3.9\% of batch 64 64 , so it is a cheap batch to deploy at. Memory is what separates the families. At the protocol batch every forward-only method fits, peaking between 1603 1603 and 1751 1751 MB, and none of the four backprop-based methods does: TENT exhausts memory and a batch- 32 32 retry hard-reset the board, because on Tegra the GPU allocates from system RAM and exhausting it starves the kernel rather than raising a clean CUDA OOM. At batch 16 16 TENT, EATA and SAR do fit, at 3300 3300 – 3306 3306 MB against QuAR’s 910 910 MB, a 3.6 × 3.6\times gap, while SPA still does not: the kernel’s OOM killer terminated it at 4256 4256 MB resident, with the triggering request arriving through Tegra’s allocator, so of the eleven methods SPA is the only one that runs at batch 1 1 alone. Batches 2 2 , 4 4 and 8 8 were not measured. Probing this safely needs one precaution, since a bare attempt can take the board down: capping the caching allocator first, here to 4200 4200 of 7486 7486 MB, leaves the kernel enough to survive and lets the OOM killer terminate only the process, which also leaves a record where a reboot would leave none.

blocks.en: Appendix S Relation to backprop-based test-time adaptation
blocks.zh: 附录S 与基于备份的测试时间适应的关系

blocks.en: Our comparison set (Table 1 ) targets the TTA methods that run on the same frozen, quantized graph as inference, which are backprop-free and use at most a few forward passes, making them realistic candidates for quantized edge deployment. A second, larger family is backprop-based – it backpropagates an unsupervised loss and updates model parameters: entropy-minimization adaptation (TENT ( Wang et al., 2021 ) , EATA ( Niu et al., 2022 ) , SAR ( Niu et al., 2023 ) ), multi-layer activation-moment matching (ActMAD ( Mirza et al., 2023 ) ), and auxiliary self-supervised feature alignment (TTT++ ( Liu et al., 2021 ) ). Table 36 contrasts the two families. Backprop-based methods are structurally ill-suited to quantized inference: (i) they require backpropagation through the (fake-)quantized graph, which the integer inference kernels of quantized accelerators do not implement; (ii) they carry an optimizer plus gradient and activation buffers; and (iii) they overwrite model parameters, which on a quantized model means re-quantization or full-precision shadow weights and risks drift over a long stream. We therefore do not use these as primary baselines; we nonetheless run four of them (TENT, EATA, SAR, and SPA ( Niu et al., 2025 ) ) on the same W6A6 model with their official code and hyperparameters (Table 7 ). Each requires an added straight-through estimator to make the frozen quantized graph differentiable. Even granted that, the three lightweight ones do not reach Ours’s backprop-free, single-forward accuracy. SPA does exceed it, at the cost of three forward passes and a backward pass per batch and a peak memory footprint that no longer fits the edge devices that quantization targets. We do not tabulate ActMAD. It is full-model test-time training that updates all parameters by gradient (and likewise needs the added STE), a far heavier regime than the lightweight TTA compared here.

blocks.en: QuAR shares with ActMAD the premise that per-channel activation moments are the quantity to align at test time, and departs from it in what is aligned, where, and how much. ActMAD aligns by descending a matching loss, so its correction is realized in the model parameters and the layers it measures are a free design choice. The local branch ( Local-only in Table 1 ) instead applies the correction as an operator on the tensor each frozen quantizer reads, which is what fixes where it has to act. Its target is therefore the quantizer’s source-calibrated operating point rather than the feature distribution itself, it matches in closed form against the same statistics that fixed those quantizers, and it matches only partially ( λ < 1 \lambda{<}1 ), where its accuracy optimum lies (Proposition U.2 ). The placement and the partial strength are both load-bearing. The same matching applied away from the late pre-quant interfaces falls below No Adapt (Table 5 ), and a full match ( λ = 1 \lambda{=}1 ) is worse than a partial one (Table 7 ).

blocks.en: Appendix T ONNX representability check
blocks.zh: 附录T ONNX 代表性检查

blocks.en: We verify that Ours is representable in a standard quantized inference graph rather than only in our PyTorch harness. Exporting the W8A8 model to ONNX (opset 17) succeeds, and each local recalibration site is exactly representable as a standard per-channel Mul / Add pair: ONNX Runtime reproduces the PyTorch logits, and the recalibration op itself matches bit-for-bit at the site level. The scale factor folds exactly into the activation quantizer, whereas the continuous per-channel shift over a per-tensor quantizer does not, so the explicit Mul / Add wrapper is the intended deployable representation; it adds one multiply and one add per recalibrated activation and updates no weights or quantizer parameters. This is a representability/executability check, not a latency, memory, or hardware claim. A full integer-only deployment with end-to-end accuracy parity, including the per-channel quantization that would let the shift fold and the aggressive W3A3/W4A4 bit-widths, is left to future work.
blocks.zh: 我们核实我们的可以代表 标准量化推论图 而不仅仅是我们的PyTorch带 将 W8A8 型号导出至 ONNX (opset 17) 成功,每个本地再校正站点作为每道Mul / Add 配对的标准完全可以代表: ONNX 运行时复制了 PyTorch logits, 重新校正操作本身在站点级别上匹配比特比特. 尺度因子完全折叠到活化量子上,而每分量子上连续的每分量子的相位移则没有,所以明显的Mul / Add 包装是预期的可部署表示;它每重排活化后会增加一乘一加并更新不重或分量子参数. 这是一种可代表性/可执行性检查,而不是暂时性、内存或硬件索赔。 完全整数的部署,并具有端到端的精度等同性,包括能使转向折叠和有侵略性的W3A3/W4A4比特-widths的每道倒数被留待未来工作.

The arguments are at the level of per-channel first and second moments and rest on the assumptions below; they are explanatory, not worst-case guarantees.

blocks.en: We analyze a simplified uniform-quantizer model . Consider one recalibrated interface and one channel c c . The frozen activation quantizer is a b b -bit uniform affine quantizer with step Δ c \Delta_{c} and clipping range [ μ s , c − α ​ σ s , c , μ s , c + α ​ σ s , c ] [\mu_{s,c}-\alpha\sigma_{s,c},\ \mu_{s,c}+\alpha\sigma_{s,c}] calibrated on source data , where α \alpha is the calibration clip factor and ( μ s , c , σ s , c ) (\mu_{s,c},\sigma_{s,c}) are the source per-channel moments. This describes the activation quantizers of PTQ4ViT ( Yuan et al., 2022 ) (twin uniform quantizers; our W6A6/W8A8 setting) at every interface, and, crucially, also the { \{ qkv, proj, fc1 } \} interfaces under AdaLog ( Wu et al., 2024 ) (W4A4/W3A3): AdaLog applies its logarithmic quantizer only to the post-Softmax and post-GELU activations, so among our recalibration interfaces only the post-GELU input to mlp.fc2 is log-quantized, and only at W4A4/W3A3. The uniform model below therefore applies directly to three of the four module types at all bit-widths; the single log-quantized interface is treated separately in paragraph (iv) (Proposition U.4 ). We assume: (A1) activation shift is captured by the per-channel mean and variance, i.e. the standardized activation ( x c − μ ⋅ , c ) / σ ⋅ , c (x_{c}-\mu_{\cdot,c})/\sigma_{\cdot,c} has an approximately shift-invariant, sub-Gaussian shape; (A2) the quantizer is calibrated to the source moments as above; (A3) the running target moments ( μ t , c , σ t , c ) (\mu_{t,c},\sigma_{t,c}) track the test stream (slowly varying); (A4) the source moments are representative of the calibration distribution; and, used only for the optimality statement in paragraph (ii), (A5) the frozen path from the interface to the logits is calibrated to be accurate at the source operating point, with expected task loss increasing locally quadratically in the per-channel operating-point deviation. (A1) is the standard covariate-shift premise behind test-time batch-norm statistic adaptation ( Schneider et al., 2020 ) .

blocks.en: Which term operates in practice. Empirically the clipping term is negligible at the tested bit-widths (activation saturation is ≤ 0.1 % \leq 0.1\% at W6A6 and ≈ 3 % \approx 3\% at W4A4, and recalibration does not reduce it), so the operative restored quantity is the code distribution rather than a lowered clipping rate. Neither figure is surprising. At W6A6 the calibrated clip edges sit between 5.5 5.5 and 18.6 18.6 source standard deviations from the mean at the recalibration interfaces, while the shift the corruptions produce is 0.082 ​ σ 0.082\sigma in the mean and a contraction of the scale to 0.92 0.92 of its calibrated value, both measured per channel against that channel’s own source scale, so the distribution never approaches the edges and the tail mass beyond them is unchanged either way. At W4A4 the edges are much closer, sixteen levels forcing calibration to trade clipping for a finer step, but the 3 % 3\% is then the rate the quantizer was calibrated to have: recalibration returns the activation to the source operating point, and that point clips at 3 % 3\% . Restoring the clipping probability and lowering it are different things, and Lemma U.1 claims only the first. Two facts fix which part of the mismatch is doing the work. The granular error power Δ c 2 / 12 \Delta_{c}^{2}/12 is set by the frozen step and no test-time correction can change it, so what recalibration can move is where the activation sits on the code grid and how many of its levels each channel occupies, not how finely that grid is spaced. And the mismatch is dominated by position: at the recalibration interfaces the per-channel mean deviation is 0.235 0.235 against 0.112 0.112 for the scale (Table 29 ), a factor of 2.1 2.1 . These are activation units rather than the per-channel σ \sigma used just above, which is the comparison that matters for the code distribution: one step Δ \Delta serves every channel of an interface, so the two components are already on a common scale and dividing each by its own σ \sigma would compare quantities the quantizer never sees separately. A mean offset leaves the granular error power untouched while relocating the activation on the frozen grid, which is precisely what the code distribution registers and what the frozen downstream weights see.

It is a ratio of sums, ∑ c σ c 2 \sum_{c}\sigma_{c}^{2} against d ​ Δ 2 / 12 d\,\Delta^{2}/12 , so it is invariant to how a fixed total activation energy is allocated across channels, whereas the resolution each channel actually receives is a per-channel quantity (Proposition 1 ). The two disagree on this stream. Corruption costs 0.53 0.53 dB of aggregate SQNR at these interfaces and QuAR leaves it essentially where it finds it ( − 0.06 -0.06 dB), yet per channel 20.6 % 20.6\% lose at least half a bit of code resolution and 4.8 % 4.8\% lose a full bit, which QuAR cuts to 6.9 % 6.9\% and 0.3 % 0.3\% (Table 38 ). The aggregate figure understates the per-channel degradation by 4.5 × 4.5\times , and the understatement is not a small-denominator artifact: restricting to channels above the median source scale raises it rather than removing it. What the corruption does to these interfaces is under-fill them, the summed per-channel second moment falling to 0.92 0.92 of its calibration value at 15 15 of the 16 16 interfaces, which is a displacement of the operating point and not a coarsening of the grid. The failure is positional, and so is the correction.

blocks.en: Where the starvation lives. It is not spread over the interfaces. Splitting them by whether a LayerNorm sits immediately before the quantizer separates them completely (Table 39 ): at the interfaces that follow one, attn.qkv after norm1 and mlp.fc1 after norm2 , not a single channel loses half a bit, and the worst loses 0.31 0.31 . The starvation is confined to the two interfaces with no normalization in front of them, the attention output and the post-GELU input, where 28.9 % 28.9\% of channels pass that threshold and the worst loses 2.51 2.51 bits. This is consistent with the normalization returning the activation to a scale close to the one the quantizer was calibrated for before it is quantized, leaving the frozen grid its calibrated fill; we report it as an observation about where the mechanism operates rather than as a further claim. The head input is post-LayerNorm and behaves accordingly, losing 0.003 0.003 bits on average under No Adapt with no channel past 0.07 0.07 . No compared method takes any head channel past half a bit either, the largest excursion any method produces at a post-LayerNorm interface being 0.46 0.46 bits, against 3.71 3.71 at an unnormalized one. The two post-LayerNorm groups were checked for all nine configurations, so this is measured rather than inferred from where each method writes; T3A, which touches only the classifier, reproduces the No-Adapt head statistics exactly.

blocks.en: Is restoring the resolution worth anything? Proposition 1 predicts that matching the scale , as opposed to only recentering, should be worth more where resolution has actually been forfeited. Because the two interface groups are disjoint, this can be tested within each group, which holds module type, width and depth fixed and toggles only whether the scale is matched. At W6A6 with the local branch alone, against No Adapt’s 47.68 47.68 : recentering only ( mean ) gives 50.21 ± 0.07 50.21\pm 0.07 at the eight post-LayerNorm interfaces and 49.77 ± 0.04 49.77\pm 0.04 at the eight unnormalized ones, and adding the rescale ( mean+var ) gives 51.25 ± 0.05 51.25\pm 0.05 and 52.49 ± 0.08 52.49\pm 0.08 , all 3-seed. The rescale is therefore worth + 1.04 +1.04 where no resolution was lost and + 2.72 +2.72 where 28.9 % 28.9\% of channels forfeited half a bit or more, a factor of 2.6 2.6 , and the unnormalized group alone accounts for 97 % 97\% of the rescale’s effect over all sixteen ( + 2.79 +2.79 ). Recentering runs the other way, worth more at the post-LayerNorm interfaces ( + 2.52 +2.52 against + 2.08 +2.08 ), where the scale is already close and the displacement is nearly a pure mean offset. The control reproduces Table 16 : recentering only over all sixteen gives 50.54 ± 0.01 50.54\pm 0.01 against that table’s 50.55 50.55 . Two limits on the reading. The + 1.04 +1.04 at the interfaces with nothing to restore shows the rescale also does something other than restoring resolution, so the + 2.72 +2.72 cannot be assigned to resolution alone; the defensible statement is the ratio, not a split of the points. And this compares a fitted quantity across groups that differ in more than resolution, which is why the comparison is made within each group rather than between them. The global branch therefore does not act by restoring code resolution, and the head’s code-distribution restoration is a displacement of the mean rather than of the scale. Proposition 1 covers the local branch, and the value-space distance of Equation 3 , which moves with both, is what covers both.

blocks.en: We deliberately stop there and do not convert bits into accuracy points: the bit-width exchange rate prices a change of precision across the whole network, including the weights and every interface we leave alone, so it cannot price a local statistic at sixteen activation interfaces, and accuracy is not linear in log-power either. The claim Proposition 1 supports is directional, that a frozen grid can only lose resolution when the activation contracts and that the lost resolution caps what those channels can carry, and that is the claim the table tests.
blocks.zh: 我们刻意停留在那里,不将比特转换成精确点:比特width汇率价格是整个网络精度的变化,包括权重和我们留下的每一个接口,因此它不能在16个激活界面上给本地统计数据定价,准确性在对数力上也不是线性的. 索赔建议1支持的是方向性,一个被冻结的网格只有在启动合同时才能失去解析度,失去的解析度封顶了这些通道能够携带的东西,这就是索赔表测试.

blocks.en: Measuring the quantizer code-distribution distance to source on the deployed adapter over the full ImageNet-C stream (5000 images per corruption), at the 17 17 recalibration interfaces (blocks 8–11 × \times { attn.qkv , attn.proj , mlp.fc1 , mlp.fc2 } and the head input) recalibration cuts this distance by 52 % 52\% (W6A6, all 15 corruptions, 3 seeds), i.e. it restores the quantizer’s code usage toward its source calibration. The two interface groups behave differently and both are covered: over the 16 intermediate interfaces the local branch removes 47.2 % 47.2\% of the drift where no baseline exceeds 1.5 % 1.5\% , and at the head input, the one interface NEO and FOA also act at, the global branch removes 90.0 % 90.0\% against their 20.6 % 20.6\% and 48.0 % 48.0\% . Only QuAR is high in both. That head ordering is the scale correction made visible: NEO subtracts a running test mean and never references the source, FOA shifts by the source mean but not the scale, and QuAR matches both. The code-distribution restoration is the quantization-specific manifestation of the moment alignment, and Proposition U.1 below makes its link to accuracy precise, bounding the quantization error’s contribution to the logits. This restoration is specific to matching the source statistics. ZOA, the one baseline designed for the quantized setting, adapts LayerNorm affine parameters against a feature-discrepancy objective rather than acting at the quantizer, and barely moves the code distribution (episodic, same interfaces, − 4.0 % -4.0\% versus Ours’s − 51.7 % -51.7\% ); T3A leaves it exactly unchanged, FOA and NEO move it only through the head interface ( − 5.6 % -5.6\% and − 2.2 % -2.2\% overall), and FOZO increases it ( + 11.8 % +11.8\% ) (Figure 1 b).

blocks.en: Table 40 breaks the Figure 1 b summary down by corruption. QuAR restores the quantizer code distribution toward its source calibration on every one of the 15 corruptions (from + 32.1 % +32.1\% on elastic transform to + 61.6 % +61.6\% on contrast), and the restoration is highly stable across seeds (std ≤ 1.2 % \leq 1.2\% per cell). The baselines do not. T3A is exactly 0 % 0\% on every corruption, as it rewrites the classifier’s decision rule and leaves every activation in the network untouched. NEO, FOA and ZOA move the distribution only slightly in the mean ( + 6.2 % +6.2\% , + 8.1 % +8.1\% , + 5.7 % +5.7\% ), and almost all of that comes from the head interface where they act; over the 16 intermediate interfaces they sit at 1.5 % 1.5\% or below. FOZO makes it worse ( − 14.8 % -14.8\% mean), as re-optimizing the model or prompts is not aligned with the frozen quantizers’ calibration. This is the direct, per-corruption evidence that the quantizer-level mismatch is a real and otherwise-unaddressed failure mode, and that QuAR’s pre-quant recalibration is what targets it.

blocks.en: This isolates why the gain concentrates on quantized models (Figure 1 a): the term it acts on, { e ℓ } \{e_{\ell}\} , exists only under quantization, and on a frozen quantizer its power cannot be reduced at all, only returned to the source operating point by moving the activation back into the calibrated range, which is precisely what the code-distribution restoration of Figure 1 b measures. Two caveats keep the claim honest. First, the bound is on the quantization error alone; the recalibration’s own estimation error (the η \eta of Proposition U.2 ) adds a competing term, so it is minimized at the shrinkage optimum λ ⋆ \lambda^{\star} , not at maximal restoration. This is measurable: the full local match ( λ = 1 \lambda{=}1 ) restores 84.2 % 84.2\% of the code-distribution drift against QuAR’s 51.7 % 51.7\% , and scores 53.52 53.52 against 54.35 54.35 (Table 7 ). The metric is therefore not a proxy for accuracy, and the configuration that maximises it is not the one to deploy. Second, restoring the code distribution is necessary to remove { e ℓ } \{e_{\ell}\} but not by itself sufficient for accuracy, which also requires the corrected activation to remain a faithful estimate of the test signal; the two hold together only for a stable, partial correction (made precise in Corollary U.2 ).

blocks.en:
Adopt the hypotheses of Proposition U.1 and model the path from interface ℓ \ell to the
logits as a fixed K > ℓ K_{>\ell} -Lipschitz map (i.e. hold the downstream quantization errors fixed, or
absorb their first-order change into K > ℓ K_{>\ell} ). Then an additional activation-space residual of
norm r ℓ r_{\ell} at interface ℓ \ell enlarges the logit-perturbation bound ‖ z ^ − z ‖ ≤ ∑ ℓ K > ℓ ​ ‖ e ℓ ‖ \|\hat{z}-z\|\leq\sum_{\ell}K_{>\ell}\|e_{\ell}\| by at most one further term, K > ℓ ​ r ℓ K_{>\ell}\,r_{\ell} .
Hence, for a fixed per-interface residual, its bounded contribution to the logit perturbation scales
with the downstream gain K > ℓ K_{>\ell} .

Under the fixed-downstream-map model, the residual r ℓ r_{\ell} propagates to the logits through the
same K > ℓ K_{>\ell} -Lipschitz composition as the quantization error e ℓ e_{\ell} in
Proposition U.1 ; by the triangle inequality its contribution to ‖ z ^ − z ‖ \|\hat{z}-z\| is at most K > ℓ ​ r ℓ K_{>\ell}\,r_{\ell} , an additional term of the same form.
∎

So the downstream gain K > ℓ K_{>\ell} controls how much an imperfect correction at ℓ \ell can perturb the logits: it bounds the risk of intervening at ℓ \ell . We probe K > ℓ K_{>\ell} with an empirical local proxy (Figure 6 ): injecting a controlled perturbation at each block input and reading the induced logit change. This proxy generally decreases with depth, from ≈ 0.26 \approx\!0.26 averaged over the early blocks (0–3) to ≈ 0.059 \approx\!0.059 over the late blocks (8–11), a ∼ 4.4 × \sim\!4.4\times attenuation (near-monotone, with one small reversal); propagated through the quantized downstream the same proxy falls from > 1 >\!1 at early blocks, i.e. genuine amplification, to < 1 <\!1 at late blocks. A correction at a late interface therefore has its residual attenuated most before reaching the head, while the same correction placed early is weighted by a much larger K > ℓ K_{>\ell} , so its residual, and any error it injects into the activation that the downstream quantizers then re-quantize, is amplified toward the logits. This is the risk-side counterpart of the empirical collapse of early- and middle-block recalibration below No Adapt (Table 5 ). The bound identifies the late blocks as the lower-risk site for an imperfect correction; the accuracy benefit and the number of blocks are determined empirically (the four-block plateau; Appendix F ).

The fixed source anchor is the key difference from optimizer-based test-time adaptation. Methods that update parameters online from an unsupervised objective (entropy minimization ( Wang et al., 2021 ) or the zeroth-order LayerNorm updates of ZOA ( Deng et al., 2025 ) ) have no such anchor: their iterate θ ( k ) = θ ( k − 1 ) − γ ​ ∇ ^ ​ ℒ ( k ) \theta^{(k)}=\theta^{(k-1)}-\gamma\,\widehat{\nabla}\mathcal{L}^{(k)} accumulates the error of the unsupervised gradient and can drift away from θ ( 0 ) \theta^{(0)} , which is why long-stream stability needs explicit safeguards (Fisher anti-forgetting in EATA ( Niu et al., 2022 ) , sharpness/entropy gating in SAR ( Niu et al., 2023 ) , a domain memory in ZOA ( Deng et al., 2025 ) ). QuAR stays source-anchored with bounded running state, matching the flat per-round trajectories in Table 2 .

Two caveats keep this honest. First, the recentering ( μ \mu -shift) and AdaLog’s learned β \beta make the linear-to-log map only approximately additive, so we treat the residual mean correction as a first-order perturbation and read the restoration as driven by the scale match (consistent with λ \lambda acting on the variance). That model has no activation quantizer, so the shift enters only through the input second moment, which a zero-mean δ \delta can only inflate; the excess it describes is the weight-step counterpart of the granular floor Δ 2 / 12 \Delta^{2}/12 in Proposition U.1 , which recalibration leaves unchanged. blocks.en: Quantizer coverage is as follows. The uniform model (Lemma U.1 and Proposition U.1 ) applies exactly to PTQ4ViT (W6A6/W8A8, all interfaces) and directly to the { \{ qkv, proj, fc1 } \} interfaces under AdaLog (W4A4/W3A3), which stay uniformly quantized; the only log-quantized recalibration interface, post-GELU mlp.fc2 , is covered by Proposition U.4 . Consistently, the symmetric-code restoration we report is measured on all 17 17 recalibration interfaces at W6A6 ( 52 % 52\% ), and QuAR is the best adapter at every bit-width where the quantizer yields a usable model (Appendix N ). The remaining limitation is that all results are first-order, moment-level statements under (A1)–(A4): they explain the observed mismatch reduction, the λ < 1 \lambda<1 optimum, and the absence of drift, but do not bound the residual error when the standardized shape itself changes (shifts that alter higher moments or inter-channel correlations), which we leave to future work.
